correctness.rationale: M^T J=JM with J=diag(I_p,-I_q) implies R=-M^-1 J symmetric and MR=R M^T=-J. Uniqueness of the stable Lyapunov solution gives S=alpha S0+beta R, current Q=alpha Q0. Expanding the positive-current trace using the Lyapunov identity yields Phi=tr(M^T D^-1 M S)+tr(M); M^T J=JM cancels mixed terms, leaving alpha^2/(Tplus*Tminus) Phi(1,1). Phi(1,1)=0 forces M symmetric, hence B=0. This reconstructs all dimensions, no commutativity A,C needed. Independently solved Lyapunov equations and EPR in twelve nontrivial cases (p,q)=(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(3,2) under three temperature contrasts; all matched scalar factor within 2e-9. Scalar matrix proof, not these finite cases, establishes universality.

value.rationale: A dimension-independent factor for a constrained but natural class of coupled Gaussian networks, valid with noncommuting internal relaxations, is structurally useful: it separates architecture/drift optimization from thermal contrast and gives an exact strict dissipation penalty.

limitations: All coordinates even time-reversal parity; two group-isotropic baths and symmetric within-group damping mandatory.
The drift-independent temperature multiplier does not hold for arbitrary nonsymmetric within-block drifts or odd-parity inertial velocities.
